Subject: DPA redlines + TOMs questions (encryption / KMS / subprocessors)

Marissa —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our legal & infosec teams reviewed and attached a redline (FinServ_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). High-level asks:

- We need clarification on encryption at rest key ownership. Our policy prefers customer-controlled keys (bring-your-own-key) for full-disk / object storage.
- Please confirm whether Redwood supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in an HSM (we can accept KMS with HSM-backed keys).
- The TOMs exhibit currently lists generic access controls — can you expand on admin separation, privileged access reviews, and the ability to supply audit logs for access to plaintext?
- We have a mandatory subprocessors clause: please confirm the full subprocessor list and notify cadence for new subprocessors; we also want a commitment to either 30-day notice or approval workflow.
- Cross-border: we need to reference SCCs (or equivalent) and any certifications that cover transfers out of the EU if relevant.

Our target is to complete DPA execution next week if these are addressed. We also prefer DocuSign execution (single-signature flow).

Can your team review the attached and summarize which items you can accept, which need alternate language, and which are non-starters?

Thanks,
Laura

Head of Legal Ops, FinServ Solutions

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the detailed redlines and the TOMs callouts. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Evelyn (security) to propose precise language and operational details.

Initial responses:
- Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) for object storage and model payloads via our KMS integration. We can offer HSM-backed keys through our enterprise key-management add-on; I'll confirm exact phrasing for the DPA.
- Envelope encryption: supported for sensitive payloads; we can include an exhibit that defines envelope flows and responsibilities.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a living list; we will provide a snapshot and commit to 30 days' notice before onboarding new subprocessors (or an approval process for critical categories).
- Cross-border transfers: we use standard contractual clauses for EU transfers and can reference those in the DPA.

I'll follow up with a consolidated redline from our side and a proposed TOMs exhibit with more explicit controls (admin separation, PAM, privileged access reviews, audit log retention and export). Plan to send by EOD today. If that looks good, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best,

1) CMK & HSM support: Evelyn, can you confirm which of our offerings are HSM-backed vs. software-KMS? Also want the exact customer responsibility matrix (what we manage vs. what they manage).

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: DPA redlines + TOMs questions — proposed TOMs edits

Marissa / Rishi —

I reviewed the FinServ TOMs asks and drafted specific exhibit language (see TOMs_Exhibit_v2.pdf). Summary of proposed edits:

- Encryption: Redwood supports CMK via integrations with AWS KMS (HSM-backed keys), GCP Cloud KMS (HSM-backed), and Azure Key Vault (HSM). We will add an exhibit that:
  * Specifies that customer-managed keys are supported for persisted customer data (objects) and optionally for ephemeral model payloads when configured.
  * Describes envelope encryption: data key (DEK) is generated per object/request and wrapped by the customer's KEK held in their KMS; Redwood never stores unwrapped KEKs.
- Key custody: include statement that root keys are HSM-protected and that key rotation schedule is configurable; include customer responsibilities section (key provisioning, rotation coordination, revocation).
- Access controls: add details on RBAC, least privilege, separation of duties for admin vs. operations, privileged access review cadence (quarterly), and PAM integration for emergency access (break-glass logging).
- Audit logging: we can export immutable access logs (AWS CloudTrail / equivalent) on request; propose 12 months retention as standard with options to extend. We can provide redact-friendly extracts for audit requests.
- Subprocessors: provide current list and commit to 30-day notice plus an exception process for urgent security fixes (we will notify and provide mitigations).

Open items for legal: whether the customer needs contractual wording for data key escrow (we strongly prefer not to escrow keys). Also need Rishi to confirm acceptable wording around log exports and redaction.

If legal signs off, we can incorporate these exhibit edits into the redline and push DocuSign.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: TOMs_Exhibit_v2.pdf

Laura / team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's consolidated redline, with candidate language for CMK support, envelope encryption exhibit, and the expanded TOMs wording (I marked any legal trade-offs inline). Highlights:

- We accept CMK for supported storage types. We cannot agree to key escrow. Proposed compromise language: we will integrate with customer-managed KMS and provide HSM-backed key services; customer is responsible for key provisioning and revocation notices.
- Subprocessor notifications: we accept a 30-day notice commitment for non-critical additions; for critical security patches we will provide immediate notice and mitigations.
- Cross-border transfers: we will reference SCCs and add a transfer mechanism exhibit.
- Audit evidence: we will provide SOC2 report and a quarterly access-review attestation.

If these points are acceptable, I propose we convert this redline to a DocuSign envelope and send to FinServ for signature. Marissa, Jonas — please confirm subprocessor list snapshot and attach DocuSign link when ready.

Rgds,
Rishi
